title: Introducing Sentry for Construction
body_markdown:
There are two core inspection protocols in the broader Sentry for Construction solution – Construction Monitoring and Construction Quality.


**Construction Monitoring** inspections give a weekly view of equipment installation progress. Sentry is flown remotely by the Raptor Maps’ ROC team, and reports will be delivered the following day. These reports produce counts and percent-installed figures for piles, trackers, modules, inverters, and combiners, all broken down by block. This information is geolocated in a dynamic, interactive Digital Twin of the site. These inspections will also report information on civil conditions, yielding detailed data on erosion, drainage, vegetation status, and perimeter conditions to support SWPPP compliance.


**Construction Quality** inspections are flown at low altitudes, and gather insights on every block after installation, providing highly granular quality insights for key components ahead of mechanical and electrical completion. Mechanical quality inspections look at tracker systems, searching for an array of detailed issues such as: askew bearing housing assemblies, cracked bushings, incorrect damper orientation, and driveline misalignment. Electrical quality inspections search for wire management issues, flagging anomalies on components such as junction boxes, connectors, and CAB lines.


Across both core inspection areas, all issues are automatically logged to a dynamically updated punchlist, and geolocated in the Digital Twin
